visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 more consistently shows the correct curve, inward/tangential force setup, vertical forces, and readable equations, whereas Lesson 1 omits the key horizontal friction/centripetal force in its force diagram and has several sustained moments where the derivation/calculation visuals become garbled or unclear.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 includes a well-formed quiz gate wired after act_cancellation with a real question, plausible options, and a correct answer, whereas Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functional interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 has clear, well-paced narration with spoken math rendered naturally, while Lesson 1 has no available narration transcript at all, making it impossible to credit its audio quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 is better because it provides generally timed visual cues near the referenced narration, whereas Lesson 1 has no transcript or cues to evaluate and therefore cannot demonstrate any sync, though Lesson 2 still has some defects such as missing equation-manipulation cues and a few offsets that appear early or late.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 accurately explains that static friction provides the centripetal force, derives mv^2/r = μsmg, cancels mass, and computes v = sqrt(0.8·9.8·50) ≈ 19.8 m/s, while Lesson 1 has no available transcript or script to verify any correct or pedagogically useful explanation.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a much cleaner, more legible, and visually consistent modern split layout, whereas Lesson 1 uses smaller sparse text and suffers from obvious overlapping/ghosted equation animation artifacts around t=40s and t=60s that make parts look broken despite Lesson 2 having some later clipping/scrolling issues.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents favor Lesson 2, most with very high confidence. Lesson 2 is judged more visually accurate, interactive, clearly narrated, better synchronized, conceptually correct, and more polished. The strongest factors are that Lesson 2 provides a complete and accurate explanation of static friction as centripetal force, includes functional quiz interactivity, has clear narration and timing cues, and maintains more legible visuals. Lesson 1 is repeatedly penalized for missing or unavailable transcript/interactivity materials and for visual/derivation issues, including unclear or garbled equation animations and an incomplete force diagram. Although Lesson 2 has some minor sync and polish issues, the verdicts are unanimous and strongly weighted toward Lesson 2.
